B is restrained so as to prevent proceeding beyond the circumscribing limits of the compound; Illustration 1 to BNS 127 is the lock-in case. The gold therefore moves to 127(2), its repealed counterpart moves to IPC 342 (the confinement punishment, not the restraint punishment in IPC 341), and the distractor moves to 126(2), which is now the plausible wrong answer.

question: Under the law in force in India today (after 1 July 2024), which section applies to this situation, and what is the punishment prescribed? B was subjected to sustained harassment for dowry by her husband and his family.

gold.label: husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty

trap.label: husband or relative of husband subjecting a woman to cruelty (repealed with effect from 1 July 2024)

punishment: up to three years, and fine

provenance.source: authored for the Phase G Stage 2 screen, from the official BNS-to-IPC corresponding section table
provenance.note: The three criminal codes were replaced with effect from 1 July 2024: the Indian Penal Code, 1860 by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023; the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023; and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
provenance.mapping_note: BNS 85 and 86 correspond to IPC 498A and its Explanation. The official correspondence table was read only up to Chapter V here, so this pair rests on the BNS titles plus the standard published mapping and needs human confirmation.
